words.meaning: intended to prevent a problem before it occurs
words.example: The team added a prophylactic review step to catch billing errors before invoices went out.

words.meaning: the area of responsibility or authority assigned to a person or group
words.example: Vendor security falls within Maya's remit, so she will lead that part of the review.

words.meaning: a paid position that requires little or no actual work
words.example: The advisory role looked prestigious, but everyone knew it was basically a sinecure.

words.meaning: done mainly for appearances rather than to create meaningful change
words.example: Employees criticized the tokenistic listening session because leadership ignored every suggestion.

words.meaning: a pivotal event or moment that marks a major change
words.example: Winning that first national client was a watershed moment for the small agency.

phrases.meaning: to deliberately use up the remaining time so that no further action can be taken
phrases.example: The vendor kept asking for minor revisions, hoping to run out the clock before the contract deadline.

phrases.meaning: to finish or deal with something quickly and easily
phrases.example: Nina made short work of the backlog once she automated the repetitive steps.

phrases.meaning: to take a real personal or financial risk in an undertaking
phrases.example: The investors wanted the founders to put skin in the game instead of relying entirely on outside money.

phrases.meaning: to leave a situation unchanged and accept whatever result follows
phrases.example: The early numbers were uneven, but we decided to let it ride for another week before changing the campaign.

phrases.term: keep your head on a swivel
phrases.meaning: to stay alert and watch carefully for changes or danger
phrases.example: Keep your head on a swivel during the rollout because customer feedback may shift quickly.
